newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU lets Portugal delay telcom liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU lets Portugal delay telcom liberalisation.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday Portugal could delay the complete liberalisation of its telecommunications markets until the beginning of 2000, two years after most other countries in the European Union must act.

It said Portugal should, however, open its market for direct international GSM mobile phone connections by January 1, 1999, and allow competitors to Portugal Telecom to carry some telecoms services over their own networks by next July 1.
Furthermore, it should allow GSM operators to use "alternative infrastructure" immediately, the Commission said in a statement.
Portugal had asked to wait until July 1999 before abolishing Portugal Telecom's monopoly over telecoms infrastructure, but the Commission said that delay wasn't justified.

Unless otherwise exempted, EU countries are supposed to open their telecoms sectors to full competition by January 1, 1998. They were also supposed to allow operators such as utility companies or railways to carry already liberalised telecoms services -- data transmission, for example -- by July 1, 1996.

But EU rules gave Portugal, Spain, Ireland and Greece the possibility to ask for five-year delays and Luxembourg to request a two-year delay on the grounds they had less developed or small telecoms networks.

Portugal asked to delay full liberalisation until January 1, 2000 to give Portugal Telecom time to reorganise and the government time to complete studies on "rebalancing" tariffs to bring them in line with costs.

Lisbon also asked to delay liberalisation of alternative infrastructure for three years beyond the EU deadline, saying Portugal Telecom earned about six percent of its revenues from providing leased circuits and immediate lifting of restrictions could lead to big revenue losses.

However, the Commission said such a long delay was not warranted since market growth would compensate for any potential revenue losses and the company could continue to develop its network during the runup to the 2000 deadline.
The Commission has already endorsed a plan by Spain to fully liberalise its markets by November 30, 1998 and one by Ireland to do so by the start of 2000.
Greece has asked to wait until January 1, 2003 and Luxembourg until January 1, 2000. -- Suzanne Perry, Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
